# Miko

> Miko is a native, cross-platform UI engine for .NET. You author the UI as Razor components (`.razor`) and Miko draws every pixel with SkiaSharp — no browser, no WebView, no HTML/CSS runtime. This folder is the reference for AI agents building a Miko app: the rules below, and under `docs/` the full Miko documentation for the version this app was created with.

## Rules

<!-- miko:include rules.md -->
Miko renders Razor components natively with SkiaSharp. It looks like web development but it is **not** a browser: there is no HTML/CSS runtime, styles are C# objects, and only Miko's own elements, attributes and components exist. Check the reference before you write UI — do not assume web or Blazor behavior.

1. **Pages.** A `.razor` file under `Pages/` with `@page "/route"` is a route; routes are
   discovered at build time. Layouts inherit `LayoutComponentBase` and render `@Body`.
2. **Styles are typed C#.** Put rules in `GlobalStyles.cs` (`StyleSheet` + `CssObject` with
   selector-string keys) or bind a `Style` object: `style="@_box"`. There is no CSS text:
   `style="color:red"` does nothing. See [Styling](./docs/guide/styling.md).
3. **Elements and attributes are a fixed set.** Attribute names are lowercase, and any attribute
   not listed in [Elements](./docs/guide/elements.md) is dropped **silently** — e.g. `placeholder`
   on `<input>`, `disabled`, `<option value>`. `<select @bind>` does not show the bound value.
4. **Prefer Ionic components** for anything interactive or styled: buttons, inputs, toggles,
   lists, cards, tabs, menus, overlays. Start at [Ionic components](./docs/components/ionic/index.md);
   each component page lists **every** parameter, event and slot — if it is not in the table, it
   does not exist. They need `builder.AddIonic()` and `@using Miko.Ionic.Components`.
5. **Follow the component structure.** `IonApp` › `IonPage` › `IonHeader` / `IonContent`; many
   children only work inside their parent — see
   [Where components go](./docs/components/ionic/index.md#where-components-go). Toolbar buttons go
   in an `IonButtons` placed in the toolbar's `Start` / `End` slot.
6. **Named slots** are child elements (`<Start>`, `<End>`, …); once you use one, put the default
   content in `<ChildContent>`.
7. **Component events are parameters.** Use a component's own `EventCallback` parameters
   (`OnClick`, `OnChange`, `@bind-Value`, …). `@onclick` and other `@on…` directives work on
   elements only — on a component they compile but are ignored.
8. **Re-rendering.** A component re-renders after its own event handlers. When a child
   component's `EventCallback` changes state that a different component renders (e.g. a menu
   button opening an `IonMenu` declared in the page), call `StateHasChanged()` in that component.
   Do not use `@onscroll` / `@onpointermove` for per-frame work — see
   [Events](./docs/guide/events.md).
9. **Verify.** Build with `dotnet build` and fix every error and warning in your `.razor` files.
   If the Miko MCP server is configured (multiplatform template, `--agent claude`), run the
   simulator and inspect the live DOM and styles through it.
<!-- /miko:include -->

## Guide

- [Getting Started](docs/guide/getting-started.md): templates, layouts, running the app.
- [Project Structure](docs/guide/project-structure.md): the files of a generated app and the platform heads.
- [Razor Components](docs/guide/razor-components.md): components, parameters, child content, `@bind`, routing, layouts, `MikoAppBuilder`.
- [Elements](docs/guide/elements.md): every markup tag and the attributes it accepts. **Check before using a tag or attribute.**
- [Styling](docs/guide/styling.md): `Style`, `Length`, `Color`, `StyleSheet` + `CssObject`, selectors, cascade, inheritance.
- [Layout](docs/guide/layout.md): box model, block / inline / flex / grid, positioning, overflow, sizing.
- [Fonts & Text](docs/guide/fonts.md): font families, fallback, custom fonts.
- [Events](docs/guide/events.md): event directives, handler properties, capture / bubbling.
- [Async & Lifecycle](docs/guide/async.md): `OnInitializedAsync`, async handlers, `EventCallback`, `StateHasChanged`.
- [Native Capabilities](docs/guide/native.md): camera, clipboard, filesystem, geolocation, … through `Miko.Native`.
- [MCP Server](docs/mcp-server.md): inspect and drive the running simulator from an agent.

## Ionic components

- [Overview](docs/components/ionic/index.md): setup, conventions, where components go, utility classes.
- [Theming](docs/components/ionic/theming.md): tokens, palette, `ConfigProvider`, dark mode, mode, overriding styles.
- [Overlays](docs/components/ionic/overlays.md): modals, alerts, action sheets, popovers, toasts, loading — declarative and through controllers.

<!-- miko:component-index docs/components/ionic/ list -->
- [Accordion](docs/components/ionic/accordion.md): `IonAccordion`, `IonAccordionGroup` — Accordions are collapsible sections: each has a header row that shows or hides the content beneath it, so long pages can be organized into groups the user expands on demand.
- [Action Sheet](docs/components/ionic/action-sheet.md): `IonActionSheet` — An action sheet is a dialog that slides up from the bottom of the screen and offers a set of options.
- [Alert](docs/components/ionic/alert.md): `IonAlert` — An alert is a dialog that shows a message, or asks for a choice, on top of the app.
- [App and Page](docs/components/ionic/app.md): `IonApp`, `IonPage` — `IonApp` is the root container of an Ionic app, and `IonPage` is the root of each routed page; together they set up the screen structure every other Ionic component expects.
- [Avatar](docs/components/ionic/avatar.md): `IonAvatar` — An avatar is a circular image, usually a picture of a person or an object, shown on its own or inside a chip or an item.
- [Back Button](docs/components/ionic/back-button.md): `IonBackButton` — A back button navigates to the previous page: it pops the navigation history when there is something to pop, and otherwise goes to a default page.
- [Badge](docs/components/ionic/badge.md): `IonBadge` — A badge is a small pill of bold text, usually a count or a short status, shown next to another element to flag new or pending content.
- [Breadcrumbs](docs/components/ionic/breadcrumbs.md): `IonBreadcrumb`, `IonBreadcrumbs` — Breadcrumbs show where the user is in a hierarchy as a row of links, from the top level down to the current page.
- [Button](docs/components/ionic/button.md): `IonButton`, `IonButtons` — Buttons provide a clickable element for actions anywhere in an app.
- [Card](docs/components/ionic/card.md): `IonCard`, `IonCardContent`, `IonCardHeader`, `IonCardSubtitle`, `IonCardTitle` — Cards are raised, rounded surfaces that group related content — a header with a title and subtitle, body text, media, lists, and actions.
- [Checkbox](docs/components/ionic/checkbox.md): `IonCheckbox` — Checkboxes let the user select any number of options from a set, or switch a single option on or off.
- [Chip](docs/components/ionic/chip.md): `IonChip` — A chip is a compact, pill-shaped element for a tag, a filter, or a contact, holding text plus an optional icon or avatar.
- [Content](docs/components/ionic/content.md): `IonContent` — Content is the scrollable main area of a page, between the header and the footer.
- [Datetime](docs/components/ionic/datetime.md): `IonDatetime`, `IonDatetimeButton` — Datetime is an inline month calendar for picking a single date.
- [Floating Action Button](docs/components/ionic/fab.md): `IonFab`, `IonFabButton`, `IonFabList` — A floating action button (FAB) is a circular button that floats above the content at a corner, edge, or the center of the screen, for the screen's primary action; it can also open lists of related actions.
- [Footer](docs/components/ionic/footer.md): `IonFooter` — A footer is the bottom region of a page: a wrapper for one or more toolbars that stays below the scrolling content.
- [Grid](docs/components/ionic/grid.md): `IonCol`, `IonGrid`, `IonRow` — The grid is a 12-column flexbox layout system for arranging content in rows and columns.
- [Header](docs/components/ionic/header.md): `IonHeader` — A header is the top region of a page: a wrapper for one or more toolbars that stays above the scrolling content.
- [Icon](docs/components/ionic/icon.md): `IonIcon` — Icons display a glyph from the bundled Ionicons set, or a custom SVG, as a square box that scales with the font size and takes the surrounding text color.
- [Infinite Scroll](docs/components/ionic/infinite-scroll.md): `IonInfiniteScroll`, `IonInfiniteScrollContent` — Infinite scroll calls the app to load more data when the user scrolls near the end of a scrolling list.
- [Input](docs/components/ionic/input.md): `IonInput` — Inputs are single-line text fields with an optional label, placeholder, helper and error text, clear button, and character counter.
- [Input OTP](docs/components/ionic/input-otp.md): `IonInputOtp` — Input OTP is a row of single-character boxes for entering one-time codes such as SMS or authenticator codes.
- [Item](docs/components/ionic/item.md): `IonItem`, `IonItemDivider`, `IonItemGroup`, `IonItemOption`, `IonItemOptions`, `IonItemSliding` — Items are the rows of a list: each one holds text plus optional icons, avatars, thumbnails, notes, badges, buttons, or a form control, and can be made tappable or swipeable.
- [Label](docs/components/ionic/label.md): `IonLabel` — A label is the text content of an item, or a standalone line of text styled to match Ionic components.
- [List](docs/components/ionic/list.md): `IonList`, `IonListHeader` — A list is a vertical container of rows, usually items, for content such as settings, contacts, or search results.
- [Loading](docs/components/ionic/loading.md): `IonLoading` — A loading indicator is an overlay that shows a spinner and an optional message, and blocks interaction with the app while work is in progress.
- [Menu](docs/components/ionic/menu.md): `IonMenu`, `IonMenuButton` — A menu is a navigation drawer that slides in from the side of the screen over the current page, with a dimmed backdrop behind it.
- [Modal](docs/components/ionic/modal.md): `IonModal` — A modal is a dialog that covers the app with its own content, typically a header and scrollable content like a page, until the user dismisses it.
- [Note](docs/components/ionic/note.md): `IonNote` — A note is a short piece of muted, smaller text for metadata, such as a count, a size, or a timestamp beside a list item.
- [Picker](docs/components/ionic/picker.md): `IonPicker`, `IonPickerColumn`, `IonPickerColumnOption` — Pickers display one or more scrollable wheels of options, each with a single selected value, inline in the page.
- [Popover](docs/components/ionic/popover.md): `IonPopover` — A popover is a small floating panel that opens next to the element that triggered it.
- [Progress Bar](docs/components/ionic/progress-bar.md): `IonProgressBar` — A progress bar is a thin horizontal bar that shows how far an operation has progressed, or — when the amount is unknown — that it is still running.
- [Radio](docs/components/ionic/radio.md): `IonRadio`, `IonRadioGroup` — Radios let the user pick exactly one option from a set.
- [Range](docs/components/ionic/range.md): `IonRange` — Ranges are sliders for picking a number between a minimum and a maximum by dragging a knob along a bar.
- [Refresher](docs/components/ionic/refresher.md): `IonRefresher`, `IonRefresherContent` — The refresher provides pull-to-refresh on a scrolling content area: pulling down from the top reveals an indicator, and releasing far enough starts a refresh.
- [Reorder](docs/components/ionic/reorder.md): `IonReorder`, `IonReorderGroup` — Reorder lets the user drag items of a list into a new order by a handle.
- [Searchbar](docs/components/ionic/searchbar.md): `IonSearchbar` — Searchbars are rounded search fields with a search icon, a clear button, and an optional cancel button.
- [Segment](docs/components/ionic/segment.md): `IonSegment`, `IonSegmentButton`, `IonSegmentContent`, `IonSegmentView` — Segments display a row of buttons, of which exactly one is selected, for switching between views or filters within a page.
- [Select](docs/components/ionic/select.md): `IonSelect`, `IonSelectOption` — Selects are form controls that let the user pick one or several values from a set of options; tapping the select opens an overlay listing the options.
- [Skeleton Text](docs/components/ionic/skeleton-text.md): `IonSkeletonText` — Skeleton text is a gray placeholder bar shown in place of text or media while the real content loads.
- [Slides](docs/components/ionic/slides.md): `IonSlide`, `IonSlides` — Slides is a swipeable carousel that shows one slide at a time, with optional arrows, pagination bullets, a scrollbar, autoplay, looping, and a fade effect.
- [Spinner](docs/components/ionic/spinner.md): `IonSpinner` — A spinner is an animated indicator that shows something is loading or in progress, with no measure of how far along it is.
- [Tabs](docs/components/ionic/tabs.md): `IonTabBar`, `IonTabButton`, `IonTabs` — Tabs are a top-level navigation pattern: a tab bar of buttons at the bottom (or top) of the screen switches between independent root pages.
- [Text](docs/components/ionic/text.md): `IonText` — Text is an inline wrapper that colors the text inside it with a palette color, for anything from a single word to a whole heading.
- [Textarea](docs/components/ionic/textarea.md): `IonTextarea` — Textareas are multi-line text fields with an optional label, placeholder, helper and error text, and character counter.
- [Thumbnail](docs/components/ionic/thumbnail.md): `IonThumbnail` — A thumbnail is a square preview image, typically shown at the start or end of a list item.
- [Title](docs/components/ionic/title.md): `IonTitle` — A title is the text label of a toolbar, naming the current screen or section.
- [Toast](docs/components/ionic/toast.md): `IonToast` — A toast is a short, non-blocking notification that appears at the top, middle, or bottom of the screen, typically to confirm an action or report a status.
- [Toggle](docs/components/ionic/toggle.md): `IonToggle` — Toggles are switches that turn a single option on or off.
- [Toolbar](docs/components/ionic/toolbar.md): `IonToolbar` — A toolbar is a horizontal bar that holds a title, buttons, and other controls for the current screen, usually placed in an `IonHeader` or `IonFooter`.
<!-- /miko:component-index -->
